title: Marked-Voronoi Limits for Nearest-Neighbor ATE Matching with Vanishing Boundary Propensity

gap_reasons: The delivered proofs establish the original-record marked-cell limit, heterogeneous-regression remainder control, and feasible conditional calibration; the bottleneck described in the brief is addressed in the stitched note. The contribution remains confined to exact scalar matching with uniform covariates, binary outcomes, and the quantitative single-boundary propensity class, rather than a general weak-overlap matching theory. The closest fixed-match Gaussian theorem imposes strong overlap and excludes this regime ([Chen–Han, Assumption 3.2(ii)](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.05758v2)); the note does not establish a recognized open-problem resolution or broadly applicable framework. I find no stale theorem-level overclaim: minimax optimality and the exponent-one transition are explicitly outside the delivered results. The projected score is constrained by that scope and the absence of reproducible finite-sample inference evidence, especially for the logarithmic simulation budget: even with an independent continuous exact reference, twenty draws give only 19/21 coverage for the stated empirical-quantile 95% interval, despite eventual asymptotic validity. proof_attempt_summary: Derived the original-record Bernoulli–Voronoi matching law and uniform conditional inference, extended the exponent range to fixed public compact subsets of (1, infinity), and reduced simulation-plus-preprocessing work to O(n log n). D0.5 mathematics and rubric passed after exact Massart source attestation, but the general referee and independent high consult found the contribution subfield with no bounded field-tier repair. Banking stops before F1: no Lean formalization, type-checker certificate, or accepted result is claimed; positioning/ballast hygiene and finite-budget coverage caveats remain recorded in the receipts.
tldr: Uncorrected scalar one-neighbor ATE matching with replacement has a primitive-derived marked-Voronoi limit when treatment probability vanishes as \(c x^\kappa\) at the covariate boundary. The theorem is uniform for fixed public \(1<\kappa_{\mathrm{lower}}\le2\le\kappa_{\mathrm{upper}}<\infty\), with unknown amplitude, exponent, and Lipschitz binary-outcome means. The error, squared reuse scale, and treated point measure converge jointly to a centered Bernoulli cell series and its geometry; bias is \(O_P(h_{P,n}^2)=o_P(h_{P,n})\). Observed geometry and an endpoint pilot give uniform conditional calibration, nominal coverage with exactly \(B_n=\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil\) independent draws, and informative \(O_P(h_{P,n})\) diameter. The complete implementation costs \(O(n\log(n+1))\) scalar operations and \(O(n)\) storage. The legal exponent-two witness has a non-Gaussian error limit; exponent one requires a separate transition theorem.
gap: Abadie--Imbens fixed-match asymptotic normality and scalar variance theory, and Chen--Han fixed-match limit theory, require overlap. Their Gaussian mechanisms do not determine the persistent \(h_{P,n}\)-scale boundary reuse array. Reuse-aware bootstrap architecture and weak-overlap IPW limits leave this matching array and its binary reference law uncharacterized.
fill: A primitive whole-array coupling and spatial tail result identify the joint law indexed by \((\kappa,p)\). Cell quadrature controls uncorrected matching bias at order \(h_{P,n}^2\); conditional mark localization, pilot transfer, anti-concentration, and dependence-safe finite-draw quantile inversion yield feasible inference. The legal witness \(P^\dagger\) distinguishes persistent, non-self-averaging marked cells and non-Gaussian error from the overlap-based Gaussian mechanisms.
